title: Climate-smart fisheries management
bottleneck: Fish stocks are shifting poleward and deeper as oceans warm, but management is built on static stock boundaries and historical baselines: quotas allocate fish that have moved to other jurisdictions, triggering conflicts, while the productivity of stocks in warmer, more acidic, less oxygenated water is poorly understood. Data-poor fisheries — most of the world's — have no assessments at all. No management framework handles rapid, directional range shifts.
why_it_blocks: Fisheries feed 3 billion people with animal protein; mismanaged shifts mean collapsed stocks, food insecurity, and fishing wars. The governance lag turns a biological response into a human crisis.
current_state: Dynamic ocean management using real-time data is being piloted for some fleets, and a few treaties have begun sharing shifting stocks. But the dominant regime remains fixed quotas for moving fish — a system designed for a stable climate.
